ACADEMY V2.1 · METHODOLOGY & ACCOUNTABILITY

How I learn and build evidence

A professional security record separates actions performed from conclusions inferred, proposed or not yet verified. I combine official guidance, scoped labs, measurable acceptance criteria and coaching feedback. Frameworks add structure; they are not certifications or audit results.

Understand first. Test safely. Then make evidence-led decisions.

My learning process

A repeatable five-stage approach.

  1. 01

    Learning objective and scope

    Describe the problem, prerequisites, scope, authorization and observed baseline.

  2. 02

    Sources and hypotheses

    Use authoritative vendor and framework guidance. State assumptions and the expected observations before testing.

  3. 03

    Safe execution

    Read-only when feasible. Changes require explicit authorization, a bounded pilot, dependency checks and a recovery plan.

  4. 04

    Validation and evidence

    Compare expected versus effective state. Where meaningful, run positive and negative tests including exclusions and failure conditions.

  5. 05

    Review and assessment

    Record uncertainty, residual risk and follow-up. Module assessments contain five independently answered questions, scored 0–4 each with coaching feedback: internal learning measurement, not an external qualification.

From observation to technical evidence

These elements apply as appropriate; not every record has completed this cycle.

01

Scope and authorization

Purpose, date, test environment, baseline and permitted actions.

02

Traceable observation

Source, method and sanitized result such as dsregcmd, an Intune status or a learning-platform outcome.

03

Tests and uncertainty

Expected versus actual behavior, negative tests, limitations and plausible alternative explanations.

04

Conclusion and recovery

Engineering decision, impact, residual risk, recovery procedure and validation still required.

What does each evidence state mean?

A configured policy is not yet proof of an effective security control.

01

Learner-observed

A lab result documented by the learner, not an independent audit.

02

Externally confirmed

A specific challenge accepted by a learning platform; not proof of full security-control effectiveness.

03

Not verified

Effective policy application, ESP completion or another essential control test is still missing.

04

Planned

A design with exit criteria, but no implementation or executed test evidence.

Frameworks as engineering references

A reference is used for a specific task or outcome; it does not confer an endorsement.

01

NIST NICE — knowledge and skills

NIST SP 800-181 Rev. 1 and separately maintained NICE Components v2.2.0 (28 April 2026) include Task, Knowledge and Skill statements. I use them to map learning objectives and relevant practical evidence.

02

NIST CSF 2.0 — security outcomes

Govern, Identify, Protect, Detect, Respond and Recover place risks, controls and improvements in context. I do not claim a fully implemented CSF program.

03

Microsoft Zero Trust — design principles

Verify explicitly, use least privilege and assume breach guide my Entra, Conditional Access and endpoint scenarios. A proposed control does not demonstrate enforcement.

04

MITRE ATT&CK — adversary behavior

Tactics and techniques help structure relevant detection and purple-team investigations. Mapping is not proof of detection coverage.
